docs/guidance/guidelines_v5_2_0_rc6_wiza.new: Sampling correlation update (QER-RC4, November 2026). The rho_dir, rho_sm_out and rho_sm_all options now estimate the sampling-error correlation after removing each domain-year mean. The calculation stays at PSU level, so it keeps household overlap and PSU persistence, but lasting differences between domains no longer inflate it. Direct variances that are only rounding residue are treated as zero. MFH results on same-PSU surveys therefore differ from earlier releases. In known-truth simulations of one synthetic scenario, intervals stayed too narrow in high-poverty domains and in domains with few PSUs, and UFH change intervals were conservative when the years were correlated. See the MCPE validation status note.

docs/guidance/guidelines_v5_2_0_rc6_wiza.old: the national sampling-error correlation is estimated from the full sample and combined with domain variances on the selected basis.
docs/guidance/guidelines_v5_2_0_rc6_wiza.new: the sampling-error correlation is estimated from the full sample at PSU level after removing each domain-year mean, and combined with domain variances on the selected basis. This keeps household overlap and PSU persistence, and excludes lasting differences between domains, which the model should capture.
